title: Safai Saathi change manifest
description: The machine-readable list of every change to the contract. Each entry pairs with a CHG-nnn-*.md file in this folder. The two change together, never one alone.

Update the driver app to read drivers.phoneMasked

changes.title: The user app's stack is React, not Flutter
changes.author: platform-owner

steps: The office decides one thing: keep the React PWA, or rewrite it in Flutter
If React stays, PRD-1 section 0 is corrected to describe the React stack and the platform's PRD pointer records the decision

changes.title: The user app owns collectionFeedback
changes.author: userapp-team

steps: The collectionFeedback collection is now in the core contract with the five fields every app must agree on
The user app owns the five app-only fields in .contract/extensions/userapp.json. The platform owner has already created that file and registered its hash
The user app keeps the extension file exactly as it is. If it changes, bump extensionVersion and ask the platform owner to re-register the hash

changes.title: The mock-location latch is set by a callable, not a client trip write
changes.author: platform-owner

steps: New callable flagMockLocation({ tripId }). It sets trips.mockLocationDetected = true on the caller's own open trip and returns { flagged, flaggedAt }
driverapp: replace the direct trips.mockLocationDetected write with a httpsCallable('flagMockLocation') call. The callable is in 04-functions/src/callables/tracking.ts
The callable never sets the field false. A second call on a flagged trip succeeds and writes nothing, so a retry is safe
The in-app banner stays local and offline-safe. The callable needs the network, so the app may retry it on reconnect
trip.schema.json x-writes no longer lists driverapp. The strict rules already denied the direct write

changes.title: Publish the notice read receipt
changes.author: platform-owner

steps: Write notices/{noticeId}/receipts/{driverCode} with readAt when the driver opens a notice. The doc id is the driverId claim, never a client-chosen value
Keep the session-local unread set as the fallback until the write path works. A failed write leaves the dot on; it never loses a notice
Compute the unread dot from the local cache plus the receipts that have synced, so an offline driver still sees the right state
The strict rules allow this write already. The loose PHASE 1 rules do not match the subcollection, so the receipt write only starts working after the CHG-0003 rules switch
Do not add a receipt array to the notice document. A targetType of all notice is read by every driver, so an array would grow without bound

changes.title: The complaints index for the driver app's bounded fetch
changes.author: platform-owner

steps: The platform deploys 03-rules/firestore.indexes.json. The index is additive and changes no document shape
driverapp switches the bounded query to orderBy createdAt descending only after the index is live. A missing index fails the query with FAILED_PRECONDITION, so the order of these two steps matters

changes.title: Audit who created and last changed a driver
changes.author: platform-owner

steps: upsertDriver sets createdAt and createdBy once, on create, from the server clock and the staffId claim. A client cannot send either
upsertDriver sets updatedAt and updatedBy on every update, from the same two sources
adminpanel may show the four fields. It does not have to: the change is additive
A driver record created before this change has no audit fields until its next upsertDriver write. Nothing backfills it
The driver app never reads these fields. Its own driver read stays field-restricted

changes.title: startShift clears a stale van marker instead of failing
changes.author: platform-owner

steps: No driver app code change. startShift now clears vans.currentTripId when the marker points at a missing trip, or at a trip whose status is not on_shift, then creates the new trip in the same transaction
staleMarker still fires when the marker points at a live trip of another van. An app that shows the staleMarker copy keeps it for that case
The repair is server-side, inside the startShift transaction. The client never clears the marker, because it cannot prove the trip is closed
The next driver on a van that died mid-shift now starts normally instead of waiting for a manual write

changes.title: Alert the ward inspector when a mock location is latched
changes.author: platform-owner

steps: flagMockLocation sends one notification per unique ward inspector across trips.wardIds, on topic staff_{staffId}
The push is sent only on the first latch. A retry that finds the latch already set sends nothing, so it cannot duplicate the alert
A push failure is logged and does not fail the call. The latch is the durable record
adminpanel must receive the staff_{staffId} topic after the staff token is minted and render data.type = mock_location_alert. The topic and the payload shape already exist
No new topic, no new field, no new collection

x-rules.together: Every entry pairs with its explainedIn file. They change in the same commit.
x-rules.severity: S0 emergency, S1 breaking, S2 new capability, S3 additive, S4 internal. See 02-contracts/severity-policy.md.
x-rules.priority: P0 to P4. Severity plus impact.
x-rules.migrationRequired: An S1 or S2 entry without migration.steps cannot merge.
x-rules.collectionNaming: affectedCollections names the Firestore collection, plural, so a developer can grep for it. A subcollection is named by its schema file's base name, singular, because its Firestore path is not a top-level collection. Both forms resolve, because 08-tools/check-consistency.ts maps the plural to the singular schema.
x-rules.extensionEntries: An EXT-nnn entry is one app's extension. It lives in the app's own repo and is registered in 02-contracts/extensions/registry.json. It does NOT move the core contract version, and the other apps are not notified. It carries kind, app and extensionVersion instead of contractVersion.
